newsitem.title: JAPAN: Prosecutors arrest Sakamaki, others on new warrant.
newsitem.headline: Prosecutors arrest Sakamaki, others on new warrant.

text.p: Tokyo prosecutors said on Thursday they had rearrested former Nomura Securities Co Ltd president Hideo Sakamaki and two other ex-Nomura executives on suspicion of paying 320 million yen to corporate racketeer Ryuichi Koike sometime around March 24, 1995.

The prosecutors said in a statement that Sakamaki was suspected of conspiring with the two others to give the money to Koike in exchange for a pledge by him to ensure smooth proceedings at a shareholders' meeting that was held on June 29, 1995.
The statement alleged that the money was given directly to Koike in cash at Nomura's Tokyo headquarters.
It added that the alleged acts were in violation of Japan's securities exchange law and commercial code.
The two other executives were Nobutaka Fujikura, a former managing director, and Osamu Fujita, a former senior official in charge of shareholders' meetings.

Earlier on Thursday, prosecutors said they had indicted Sakamaki on charges of making illegal payoffs to Koike of 49.73 million yen between January 31 and June 15, 1995. Fujikura had already been indicted on the same charge.
Sakamaki resigned from the top post at Nomura, Japan's biggest brokerage, in March over the scandal, which has also embroiled Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd (DKB), one of Japan's largest banks.
Nomura itself has already been indicted on suspicion of violating the securities law by compensating a firm owned by Koike's brother for trading losses.
The scandal has so far led to the arrests of five Nomura officials, 10 DKB officials and the two Koike brothers.
